lesson.title: First Volley: Build the Point
lesson.hook: Two connected choices. Watch what your first shot creates.
lesson.liveIntro: Your approach brings you in. Their passing shot dips below net height on your forehand side.

tv1A.name: How do you handle this next volley?
tv1A.sit: Their next pass comes to your backhand. You have stayed balanced near the net.
tv1A.q: How do you handle this next volley?
opts: Keep the action compact and place it deep

lines.A: You keep the racket in front and use depth. The point continues.
lines.B: The angle lands here, but the moving contact makes that small target demanding.

tv1A.take: A low first volley builds the point. Depth can earn the next ball.
tv1A.payoff: A low first volley builds the point. Depth can earn the next ball.
tv1A.principle: Low volley, compact action. Build the point, then stay ready.
tv1A.why: Split around their hit, lower with the legs and use a compact forward action. A low contact needs clearance. A short floating volley gives the passer time and space; a deep volley can restrict those options without guaranteeing an easy finish.

tv1B.name: How do you handle this next volley?
tv1B.sit: Their earlier pass comes lower and farther to your backhand. You have to adjust.
tv1B.q: How do you handle this next volley?
opts: Keep the action compact and place it deep

lines.A: You respect the lower contact and keep the ball playable.
lines.B: A small target demands more while hurried. A landing does not prove the choice.

tv1B.take: A low first volley builds the point. Depth can earn the next ball.
tv1B.payoff: A low first volley builds the point. Depth can earn the next ball.
tv1B.principle: Low volley, compact action. Build the point, then stay ready.
tv1B.why: Split around their hit, lower with the legs and use a compact forward action. A low contact needs clearance. A short floating volley gives the passer time and space; a deep volley can restrict those options without guaranteeing an easy finish.

tv1.name: What does this low first volley need?
tv1.sit: Your approach brings you in. Their passing shot dips below net height on your forehand side.
tv1.q: What does this low first volley need?
opts: Bend and guide with depth through the middle
Float a short volley toward their side

lines.A: Your compact volley gives clearance and depth. Reset for their next hit.
lines.B: The short float lets them move forward. Stay ready for a harder second volley.

summaries.11: Both choices fitted the contact and court you had. Keep reading as the point changes.
summaries.01: You adapted on the second ball. Compare what the first choice cost.
summaries.00: Compare the first choice, then read the next contact again. A landing alone does not prove a sound decision.

pro.label: Borges · Earn a manageable first volley
pro.moment: Borges links his net success to selecting a good moment to approach and making the opponent’s reply difficult. He does not treat reaching the net as the finish.
pro.read: Your next point: this first volley is low. Give it clearance and useful depth, then read whether the next ball offers a finish.
pro.src: Nuno Borges · ATP interview on his 2025 net play · January 2026
pro.note: Borges explains the approach choice. The low-volley decision here is GameSharp’s application.

drill.name: Two-ball read
drill.how: Approach a deep feed. Have the passer alternate low forehand and backhand passes. Play two volleys, valuing balance and depth before a finish.
